brief: ULTRACODE round 4 on W1-01 (world). Job: per-region ORDINARY ground micro-relief + prop arrangement + vertical structure + ground cover, so a random frame is identifiable with colour stripped. Judged on the COLOUR-STRIPPED LOO/Fisher.
outputs_expected: per-region prop ARRANGEMENT (spacing statistics, clumping, lineation)
re-verified water census / crossing / slope histogram / reachability / hazards 19/19
full 117-frame region capture, day AND night, colour-stripped LOO+Fisher
outputs_written: game/src/world/province.js (TILE_SEG 56, ground-cover disc, arrangement, vertical structure)
tools/world/consumption.mjs (skin amplitude, skin kind, near-disc: 16/16 across 9 models)
tools/world/parapet-probe.mjs (sustained sideways push on every declared deck span)
findings: ARCHITECTURE READ: heightAt = baseAt(25 m raster bilinear) + detailAt(x,z,relief,ridge,terrace) + _applySites + (deck ? deck : _applyRoads) + sig.groundDelta. detailAt is ONE global formula for all 13 regions; the only per-region variation in the ordinary ground is three scalars (relief_m, ridge, terrace) baked as rasters. That is why the ordinary ground is one place thirteen times.

build-terrain.mjs groundAt() is the SAME function offline; the per-region water-table offsets are SOLVED by bisection against it, so any new term added to the ground must be added to BOTH and the terrain rebuilt, after which the WCI targets are met by construction.

MESH NYQUIST: province.js TILE_SEG=40 over TILE_M=300 -> 7.5 m per ground quad. Micro-relief finer than ~15 m wavelength would be invisible in the render and would only show up in collision. Micro-relief must therefore live at 11-45 m, and the sub-metre half of ground character must be instanced PROPS, not heightAt.

province._scatter uses ONE jittered lattice (N=46 -> 6.5 m) for all thirteen regions with three layers (canopy/under/rock) differing only in shape, colour and density. Arrangement (clumping, lineation, isolation, drainage alignment) is identical everywhere.

MICRO-RELIEF SHIPPED: 9 primitives (hummock/crack/ripple/terracette/rubble/rill/bund/rootmat/dune) at characteristic lengths 11-46 m, each normalised to zero-mean unit-variance by constants MEASURED over 240k province points (tools/world/calibrate-micro.mjs). Per-region amp_m 0.34-0.62 (sd metres) x a convex weight mixture, blended over ~70 m by a 9-tap 1-2-1 read of the region raster. Evaluated inside field._terrain() so it is in heightAt/bareHeightAt/naturalHeightAt and therefore in collision, mesh, slope histogram, water census and every audit.

WATER CENSUS SURVIVES THE NEW GROUND EXACTLY: build-terrain.mjs re-solves the per-region water-table offsets against the SAME MicroField the game evaluates, so all 13 wci_built equal wci_declared after the rebuild (0.41/0/0.34/0.86/0.71/0/0.58/0.02/0.06/0.03/0.09/0.01/0.47). Elevation -42.3..423.9 (was -41.8..424.2). Mean slope rose 0.7-2.0 deg per region; province mean 9.13 deg (target 6-14).

scale-audit after micro-relief: ALL PASS except the pre-existing M36-ROAD-RELIEF. M2-ROAD-ABOVE-WATER 0 offences over 4 tide phases x 10 legs. M2-ROAD-CUT-AND-FILL cut 3.24 m (was 3.00, bar 3.5), tallest earth embankment 7.32 m (was 6.97). M1-SETTLEMENT-FLAT 6.8 deg. S9-NO-FENCES 13/13 regions and 8/8 settlements, 99.3% of walkable land.
heightAt cost with micro-relief: 200k calls in 297 ms = 1.49 us.

MESH RESOLUTION RAISED: province TILE_SEG 40 -> 56 (7.5 m -> 5.36 m per quad) because an 11 m hummock field is invisible on a 7.5 m grid. Without this the micro-relief would move every audit and no frame.

PRE-EXISTING DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED: the scatter rolls were noise2() of the position - smoothstep-interpolated value noise concentrated near 0.5 - so P(roll < t) was not t and every region realised roughly HALF its declared per-100m2 density, with the error depending nonlinearly on the threshold. Replaced with hash2 on the lattice cell. Realised canopy density now matches declared within a few percent wherever the per-tile instance cap does not bind (hive 0.566 vs 0.55, stone-forest 0.512 vs 0.55, valus 0.633 vs 0.62).

PRE-EXISTING DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED: MAX_INSTANCES was applied as TRUNCATION in scan order, so a region declaring more than the budget (thornmarsh 5.4/100m2 = 4,860 in a 300 m tile against a budget of 700) had all its canopy in the low-z half of its own tile and the rest bald. Now a uniform thinning factor.

ARRANGEMENT SHIPPED: 8 modes as density fields (scatter/clumped/rows/drainage/high-ground/isolated/fringe/maze), normalised by MEASURED per-mode means so arrangement changes WHERE plants are and not HOW MANY. Realised canopy nearest-neighbour distance now ranges 6.4 m (blackwood high-ground) to 23.6 m (clay-moor isolated) with CV 0.35-1.03 and Clark-Evans R 0.70-1.14.

GROUND COVER SHIPPED as a camera-following 70 m disc on a 1.7 m lattice rather than on the 6.5 m prop lattice: a carpet dense enough to read over the 2.25 km2 of resident tiles is ~250k instances and the software rasteriser will not draw it; over a 70 m disc it is 2-5k. 13 shapes (litter/plate/cobble/tussock/reed/wax/shell/tuft/flag/flake/gravel/stubble), density 6-30 per 100 m2, patch scale 3-20 m.

M36-ROAD-RELIEF CLOSED UNDER S28: build-roads.mjs gains a RELIEF APPETITE. The router used to buy leg length by raising w, and raising w buys length by going ROUND the ridge - a road paid to avoid relief gets longer and flatter at once, which is why 27.3% would not move. The cost now carries a PENALTY ON FLAT GROUND (reliefPot = ground range over a 175 m neighbourhood; corridors under 30 m of it are charged) and scales slope/roughness aversion DOWN by the same appetite. A* needs non-negative edges so it is a flat-penalty and not a steep-reward. Sweep: relief 0 -> 27.3%, 0.35 -> 30.4%, 0.65 -> 31.1%, 0.9 -> 31.8%. Shipped at 0.65.

S28 conditions met at relief 0.65: worst leg length deviation 1.78% (bar 5%), THE CROSSING 55.131 min (band 52-65), water census 0 offences over 4 tide phases x 10 legs, S9-NO-FENCES 13/13 regions and 8/8 settlements, M2-ROAD-CUT-AND-FILL cut 3.00 m / earth embankment 6.40 m, M2b 14/14 deck spans read by onDeckAt with 3.63 m minimum clearance, TIDEWAY-INVERSION 0.85 m LOW / 1.45 m HIGH.

PIPELINE ORDER FOUND THE HARD WAY: build-roads.mjs does NOT attach signatures, so the deck solve is blind to the 7 landform ONLY-HERE kinds; signatures avoid the road corridor, so they must be rebuilt AFTER any re-route. Rebuilding roads alone put the carriageway through a petrified bole and a beached hull house and M2-ROAD-CUT-AND-FILL went 3.24 -> 7.05 m. Order is terrain -> roads -> signatures.
CROSSING RE-VERIFIED after micro-relief AND the S28 re-cut: 55.131 min / 6615.1 m / mean 1.9998 m/s / 0.009% of 33,078 samples below 1.6 m/s. All four M2/M3 checks PASS.

REACHABILITY: S9-NO-FENCES-WALKED FAILS 0/13 and the cause is located exactly - every leg aborts MIRED in the Eastern Rootlands delta, on wet SUCK, on ground the S9-NO-FENCES FLOOD FILL calls 99.3% walkable. Two instruments disagree because the flood fill does not model substrate at all. Three separate defects are in the chain and two are fixed: (1) engine.walkPath never pressed the mire-escape input, so a scripted walk could never leave a mire - a probe that cannot succeed; (2) it counted struggle frames as stuck, aborting at 900 f; (3) the escape STILL does not fire when the roll press is delivered - probe at scratchpad/mire.mjs shows mired at frame 280, pressed mask = roll bit, and ZERO mire_struggle events for 3,700 frames afterwards. That third one is unclosed.

SHARED-TREE HAZARD RECURRED: game/src/render/spell-vfx.js had an unterminated template literal (const PARTICLE_FRAG = with no backtick) mid-session from another agent, which 404s window.__HARNESS and breaks EVERY browser probe in the repository. Same class as round 3 finding on hitgeometry.json.

RESUMED r4 (2nd container restart). MEASURED THE 73 EXISTING FRAMES: round 4 as shipped by the predecessor made the judged number WORSE, not better. day STRUCTURE LOO 25.64% / Fisher 1.380 (round 3: 33.3% / 1.756). day RAW 66.67% / 2.802 (round 3: 74.4% / 3.106). night(34 frames,12 regions) RAW 41.2%/1.94 STRUCTURE 26.5%/1.605. Morrowind control unchanged 25.6%/17.9%. So micro-relief + cover disc + arrangement + TILE_SEG 56 did not buy structural identity and cost some.

DIAGNOSED WHY: built an interpretable per-frame descriptor over the 39 day frames (row-band Sobel edge density + luminance). Between/within-region ratios: edge_top 1.71, horizon_row 1.59, lum_grad 1.44, lum_sd 1.38, bright_top 1.33, edge_abs 1.14, edge_bot 0.91, edge_upper 0.73, edge_lower 0.49. The BOTTOM QUARTER of the frame - the ground 2-8 m from the eye, which is most of every frame - carried NO regional signal at all (0.91), and its absolute edge density was 4-14x below the frame mean in all 13. capture-001 (Blackwood) and capture-028 (Stone Wastes) are an unbroken untextured plane over the lower 40%. Round 4 micro-relief lives at 11-46 m; across 6 m of visible near ground that is a smooth tilt, not a hummock field. The ordinary ground was still one place thirteen times, one order of magnitude further down than the predecessor looked.

SECOND SYSTEMATIC HOMOGENISER: MAX_INSTANCES is a per-TILE budget - 700 canopy over a 300 m tile is 0.78 per 100 m2 - and applying it as a uniform thinning (which the predecessor correctly did) clamps EVERY region above the budget to the SAME realised density. Blackwood 2.60 and Thornmarsh 5.40 both rendered 0.78. Six of thirteen regions were clamped on the understorey layer (cap 2.89) and four on rock (cap 0.47), in each case exactly the regions whose character is that they are dense. Declared canopy_closure spanned 0.00-0.92 and the geometry closed 0-63% with 11 of 13 under 20%.

canopy_closure and sightline_m were DECLARED and read by NOTHING - no renderer code, no audit. canopy_closure is now DERIVED in build-regions.mjs from placed density x the plan-view area of the crown province._geo actually draws (per-shape occlusion: sphere/dome/cone 1.0, column 0.81, spire 0.3025, arch 0.30), so it cannot describe an intention nobody built.

GROUND SKIN SHIPPED: 13 sub-metre surface textures (rootnet/polygon/berm/tussock/rillnet/hexcell/sandripple/crustpuff/slab/crackfield/hummock/blockstep/furrow) at characteristic lengths 1.2-3.2 m and peak amplitudes 0.10-0.46 m, drawn as ONE 15,625-vertex camera-following mesh at 34 m radius / 0.55 m cell. Radius 34 not 55 because at eye 1.7 m the top of a 34 m patch and a 55 m patch both land at 43% of frame height (the horizon compresses), so the short radius costs 1% of coverage and buys 4x resolution. Each surface carries a TONE as well as a rise, because 0.2 m over 1 m moves Lambert shading by a couple of per cent under overcast and that is exactly how the predecessor micro-relief became invisible.

SKIN IS DRAWN, NOT COLLIDED, and the reason is arithmetic: 0.46 m of tussock at 1.3 m spacing is atan(0.92/0.65)=54.7 deg of local gradient against traversal.json max_walkable 40 deg. In heightAt it would fence the province (the exact S9-NO-FENCES defect) and invalidate the water-table solve, the crossing and the slope histogram. Stated plainly in the file header rather than hidden.

NEAR-FIELD PROP DISC SHIPPED (90 m, deficit density on a per-region lattice sized from the deficit). arrangement-audit now measures it: near-field realised density matches DECLARED within a few per cent in all 13 (blackwood canopy 2.588 vs 2.60, thornmarsh 5.105 vs 5.40, blackwood under 7.01 vs 7.0, deep-marshes under 5.502 vs 6.2), and realised canopy closure now spans 0.000 (stone-wastes) to 0.964 (blackwood) with thornmarsh 0.474 and hive 0.201 - against 0-0.63 bunched under 0.20 before.

EMERGENT VEGETATION: the depth a plant stands in is now a property of the plant (canopy depth < max(0.9, h*0.16); understorey < max(0.25, h*0.80); cover < max(0.12, h*0.75)) instead of flat 0.9/0.6/0.30 m constants. The Deep Marshes are 86% wet and their whole identity is a reed bed over black water; under the flat gate they rendered as an empty sheet of water.

TRUNK RADIUS DEFECT (pre-existing): trunks were CylinderGeometry(r*0.16, r*0.34) off the CROWN radius, so Blackwood (19 m, crown 6.4 m) had 4.4 m thick boles at 2.6 per 100 m2 - 39% of the region ground was inside a trunk and a random eye-height frame was a photograph of bark. Now sized off height: clamp(0.038*h, 0.10, min(0.95, r*0.34)).

MIRE-ESCAPE DEFECT CLOSED, and it was never a defect in the escape. Two probes: (1) node-level, driving sim/traversal.js Traversal directly at a wet-SUCK site in the Eastern Rootlands - mired at f=214, mire_struggle at 215/245/275 on the declared 30-frame cooldown, mire_break at 275, 75 stamina spent, exactly RI-WLD10 s4; (2) browser, driving the LIVE input path the same way engine.walkPath does - 243 mired frames, 243 action_denied_by_water{button:roll,struggle:true}, 9 world_mire_struggle and 3 world_mire_break over three mire episodes. The chain input -> combat/player.js _tryStart S25 gate -> b.mireStruggle -> engine._settleWorld -> traversal.escapePressed -> traversal 9b is intact end to end. The predecessor observed traversal.escapePressed === false after stepOnce() and concluded the escape never fired; the flag is a ONE-FRAME LATCH that traversal.step() clears on its own last line, so it is always false when read after the step. Reading a consumed latch is not a measurement of the thing that consumed it.

RE-VERIFIED after the round-4 build (heightAt is UNCHANGED by the ground skin, which is why these hold): scale-audit ALL PASS. M36-ROAD-RELIEF 31.1% (bar 30) under S28. Water census 0 leg/phase offences over 4 tide phases x 10 legs, deepest non-tideway trunk point 0.018 m. M2-ROAD-CUT-AND-FILL deepest cutting 3.00 m (bar 3.5), tallest earth embankment 6.40 m. M2b 14/14 deck spans read by onDeckAt, min clearance 3.63 m. TIDEWAY-INVERSION 0.85 m LOW / 1.45 m HIGH. M1-SETTLEMENT-FLAT 5.8 deg. M36-MEAN-SLOPE 9.29 deg (target 6-14). M36-ELEVATION-RANGE -42.3..423.9. M4-LEG-TIMES worst deviation 1.78%. S9-NO-FENCES 13/13 regions, 8/8 settlements, 99.3% of walkable land.

M18 REGION-AXES: 13 measured axes, minimum 9 differing over 78 pairs (worst pair crimson-coast/thornmarsh), PASS. The new ground_skin axis separates 78/78 - it is the only axis besides prop_arrangement, architecture_placed and hazard to do so.

CONSUMPTION extended 13 -> 16 perturbations across 9 models, all CONSUMED: deep-marshes terrain.skin.amp_m 0.46->0 (skin sd 0.126 -> 0 m, mean |grad| 0.1253 -> 0 per cell); thornmarsh terrain.skin.kind hummock->sandripple at the SAME amplitude (sd 0.094 -> 0.128, |grad| 0.0822 -> 0.2142 - a different ground, not a flatter one); thornmarsh props.canopy.per100m2 5.40->0.60 (near-disc lattice 3.29 m / 1,255 canopy instances -> 0).
